atoms.text: This guide describes a bucket policy statement on the bucket example-clickstream-raw that lets the Quillquery SQL engine read raw clickstream files and write query results. Quillquery runs submitted queries under an IAM role named QuillqueryExecutionRole in account 111122223333. The statement names that role, arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/QuillqueryExecutionRole, as the Principal. It allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::example-clickstream-raw/input/* and allows s3:ListBucket on the bucket with an s3:prefix condition limited to input/. A second action set allows s3:PutObject and s3:AbortMultipartUpload on arn:aws:s3:::example-clickstream-raw/results/*. The role's trust policy must permit the query engine to assume it, and the role needs a matching identity-based policy if the bucket belongs to a different account. Result files are written under results/ and are attributed to the role's session in access logs. To verify the setup, run a query over a table backed by input/ and confirm that the output objects appear under results/ with the role as the requester.

This guide describes a bucket policy statement on the bucket example-clickstream-raw that lets the Quillquery SQL engine read raw clickstream files and write query results. Quillquery runs submitted queries and calls the bucket with its own service identity. The statement names the service principal quillquery.amazonaws.com as the Principal. It allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::example-clickstream-raw/input/* and allows s3:ListBucket on the bucket with an s3:prefix condition limited to input/. A second action set allows s3:PutObject and s3:AbortMultipartUpload on arn:aws:s3:::example-clickstream-raw/results/*. The statement also carries aws:SourceAccount equal to 111122223333 and aws:SourceArn matching arn:aws:quillquery:us-east-1:111122223333:workgroup/*, so only your account's workgroups can use it. Result files are written under results/ and are attributed to the service principal in access logs. To verify the setup, run a query over a table backed by input/ and confirm that the output objects appear under results/ with the service as the requester.

This guide covers a bucket policy statement for the bucket example-sales-lake used by the Gristmill batch transformation service. Gristmill jobs read partitioned Parquet files from raw/sales/ and write transformed datasets to curated/sales/. Jobs execute under an IAM role, arn:aws:iam::444455556666:role/GristmillJobRole, and that role ARN is the Principal in the statement. The statement grants s3:GetObject and s3:ListBucket for the raw/sales/ prefix. It grants s3:PutObject and s3:DeleteObject for curated/sales/ so that a job can replace its previous output during a re-run. Job definitions must reference this role at creation time, and the role needs a trust relationship that lets the batch service assume it. Output objects are stored with the role's account as the owner. After applying the policy, start a test job against a single partition and check that the curated/sales/ output is complete and that no writes were denied.

This guide covers a bucket policy statement for the bucket example-sales-lake used by the Gristmill batch transformation service. Gristmill jobs read partitioned Parquet files from raw/sales/ and write transformed datasets to curated/sales/. Jobs reach the bucket through the service's own identity, and the service principal gristmill.amazonaws.com is the Principal in the statement. The statement grants s3:GetObject and s3:ListBucket for the raw/sales/ prefix. It grants s3:PutObject and s3:DeleteObject for curated/sales/ so that a job can replace its previous output during a re-run. The statement is restricted with aws:SourceAccount set to 444455556666 and aws:SourceArn matching arn:aws:gristmill:us-west-2:444455556666:job/*. Output objects are written by the service on behalf of those jobs and are stored with the bucket owner as the owner. After applying the policy, start a test job against a single partition and check that the curated/sales/ output is complete and that no writes were denied.

This guide explains a cross-account bucket policy for the bucket example-partner-feeds, which holds delimited files delivered by a data partner. The analytics team runs the Tidewell ingestion service in account 777788889999 and needs it to read the incoming files and write validation reports. Access is granted to the IAM role arn:aws:iam::777788889999:role/TidewellIngestRole, which is named as the Principal. The statement allows s3:GetObject and s3:ListBucket on the incoming/ prefix. It also allows s3:PutObject on reports/, and the statement requires the bucket-owner-full-control canned ACL on every write. The role in account 777788889999 must hold an identity-based policy permitting the same actions, because cross-account access needs both sides to allow it. Reports are written once per file batch and are named after the batch ID. Validate the setup by dropping a small test file into incoming/ and confirming that a matching report appears in reports/.

The analytics team runs the Tidewell ingestion service in account 777788889999 and needs it to read the incoming files and write validation reports. Access is granted to the service principal tidewell.amazonaws.com, which is named as the Principal. The statement allows s3:GetObject and s3:ListBucket on the incoming/ prefix. It also allows s3:PutObject on reports/, and the statement requires the bucket-owner-full-control canned ACL on every write. The statement includes an aws:SourceAccount condition of 777788889999 and an aws:SourceArn condition for the pipeline resources in that account, which keeps other tenants of the service out. Reports are written once per file batch and are named after the batch ID. Validate the setup by dropping a small test file into incoming/ and confirming that a matching report appears in reports/.

This guide describes a bucket policy statement for the bucket example-ml-training that supports the Featurekiln feature-computation service. Featurekiln jobs read labeled training records from datasets/events/ and write computed feature snapshots to features/snapshots/. The statement names the IAM user arn:aws:iam::222233334444:user/featurekiln-batch as the Principal, because this deployment uses a dedicated user with long-lived credentials. It grants s3:GetObject and s3:ListBucket on datasets/events/. It grants s3:PutObject on features/snapshots/ and denies writes that do not use AES256 server-side encryption. The access keys of that user must be rotated on a fixed schedule and stored in the job's secret store. Snapshots are versioned, so an overwritten snapshot can be restored from a prior version. To test, run a single feature computation for one day of events and check that a snapshot object is created with encryption enabled.

This guide describes a bucket policy statement for the bucket example-ml-training that supports the Featurekiln feature-computation service. Featurekiln jobs read labeled training records from datasets/events/ and write computed feature snapshots to features/snapshots/. The statement names the service principal featurekiln.amazonaws.com as the Principal, so no long-lived credentials are involved. It grants s3:GetObject and s3:ListBucket on datasets/events/. It grants s3:PutObject on features/snapshots/ and denies writes that do not use AES256 server-side encryption. Conditions set aws:SourceAccount to 222233334444 and aws:SourceArn to arn:aws:featurekiln:eu-west-1:222233334444:computation/*. Snapshots are versioned, so an overwritten snapshot can be restored from a prior version. To test, run a single feature computation for one day of events and check that a snapshot object is created with encryption enabled.

This guide covers the bucket policy for example-billing-exports, which stores daily usage export files read by the Tallyforge reporting service. Tallyforge aggregates the exports and writes monthly summary reports back to the same bucket. Its worker process runs under the IAM role arn:aws:iam::555566667777:role/TallyforgeWorker, and the statement lists that role as the Principal. The role may call s3:GetObject on exports/daily/* and s3:ListBucket with a prefix condition of exports/daily/. It may call s3:PutObject on reports/monthly/*. Scheduled runs start on the first day of each month, so the policy has no time-based restrictions. The role's session name is recorded with each request, which helps trace report generation in access logs. After deployment, trigger a manual run for the previous month and confirm that exactly one summary object is created under reports/monthly/.

The service may call s3:GetObject on exports/daily/* and s3:ListBucket with a prefix condition of exports/daily/. It may call s3:PutObject on reports/monthly/*. The statement is bound by aws:SourceAccount set to 555566667777 and aws:SourceArn matching arn:aws:tallyforge:us-east-1:555566667777:schedule/*. Scheduled runs start on the first day of each month, so the policy has no time-based restrictions. This guide describes a bucket policy statement for example-network-telemetry, where network flow logs are stored in hourly objects. The Loglens analysis service reads these logs and writes detected anomaly findings as JSON files. The statement identifies the account itself as the Principal using arn:aws:iam::888899990000:root, which delegates access decisions to IAM policies in that account. It allows s3:GetObject and s3:ListBucket on flowlogs/. It allows s3:PutObject on findings/. Administrators then attach identity-based policies to the specific role used by Loglens, so access is narrowed beyond the bucket policy. Any other role in the account can be granted access the same way, which is a consequence of naming the account. Verify the configuration by running an analysis over one hour of logs and confirming that a findings file is written and that an unrelated role without an attached policy is denied.

This guide describes a bucket policy statement for example-network-telemetry, where network flow logs are stored in hourly objects. The Loglens analysis service reads these logs and writes detected anomaly findings as JSON files. The statement identifies the service itself as the Principal using loglens.amazonaws.com, so only that service can act under it. It allows s3:GetObject and s3:ListBucket on flowlogs/. It allows s3:PutObject on findings/. The statement is narrowed with aws:SourceAccount set to 888899990000 and aws:SourceArn matching arn:aws:loglens:us-east-2:888899990000:analyzer/*. No other principal in the account gains access from this statement, which is a consequence of naming the service. Verify the configuration by running an analysis over one hour of logs and confirming that a findings file is written and that an unrelated role without an attached policy is denied.

This guide describes a bucket policy for example-iot-readings, which receives sensor files in the inbox/ prefix. The Pulsegrid aggregation service reads each file and writes rolled-up hourly statistics to rollups/. Aggregation runs under the IAM role arn:aws:iam::333344445555:role/PulsegridAggregator, which the statement names as the Principal. The role may call s3:GetObject and s3:DeleteObject on inbox/*, so that processed files are removed after a successful rollup. It may call s3:PutObject on rollups/*. A condition requires that requests come from the organization by checking aws:PrincipalOrgID against o-exampleorg123. The role must be listed in the aggregation job configuration, and its trust policy must allow assumption by the aggregation workers. Test the policy by uploading a sample sensor file, waiting for the next aggregation cycle, and confirming that the file was removed and a rollup object was created.

This guide describes a bucket policy for example-iot-readings, which receives sensor files in the inbox/ prefix. The Pulsegrid aggregation service reads each file and writes rolled-up hourly statistics to rollups/. Aggregation runs as the service itself, and the statement names pulsegrid.amazonaws.com as the Principal. The service may call s3:GetObject and s3:DeleteObject on inbox/*, so that processed files are removed after a successful rollup. It may call s3:PutObject on rollups/*. Conditions require aws:SourceAccount equal to 333344445555 and aws:SourceArn matching arn:aws:pulsegrid:ap-southeast-1:333344445555:aggregation/*. The aggregation configuration only needs to reference the target bucket, because no role has to be assumed. Test the policy by uploading a sample sensor file, waiting for the next aggregation cycle, and confirming that the file was removed and a rollup object was created.

This guide covers a bucket policy statement for example-customer-datasets, used by the Plumbline data-quality scanner. Plumbline reads tabular datasets from datasets/ and writes profiling reports containing null counts and schema drift summaries to quality-reports/. The scanner's execution role, arn:aws:iam::666677778888:role/PlumblineScanRole, is the Principal in the statement. The statement allows s3:GetObject and s3:ListBucket on datasets/ and s3:PutObject on quality-reports/. A Deny statement blocks any write to quality-reports/ that lacks the s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption header set to AES256. Because the datasets may contain personal data, the role does not receive any delete or ACL permissions. Reports are retained for ninety days under a lifecycle rule. Confirm the setup by scanning one small dataset and checking that the report is encrypted and that attempts to read objects outside datasets/ are denied.
